overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance metrics highlights a massive viewer preference for high-concept, extreme space scenarios—particularly 'What If' hypothetical environmental scenarios and exotic exoplanet conditions (e.g., liquid diamond, extreme darkness, unusual rain mechanics). Videos utilizing speculative physics and vivid comparative scales ('What If You Fell Into...') generated the highest velocity in views, engagement, and likes-per-view over the recent 7-day window. Conversely, standard psychological facts and routine biological trivia underperformed relative to cosmic scale content.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) lead in views (1000+) and engagement within days of publishing.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical space scenarios involving extreme physical states (e.g., entering strange celestial bodies, black holes, or exotic matter).

winning_patterns.pattern: Bizarre Exoplanet Weather and Material Anomalies
winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing extreme planetary environments like 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (v1rrcZLdp4U) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (A9Qa-RmuOr0) show strong, sustained traction.
winning_patterns.action: Highlight physical contradictions or bizarre planetary conditions that defy everyday intuition using vivid descriptive adjectives.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like song memory loops (ef3ND4qiRHc, Jc04LVKNd2s) and basic animal facts (AXAfwrzzEdU) stagnate under 200 views with negligible engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standalone human psychology trivia unless framed through an extreme evolutionary or cosmic survival lens.
